title: Waves: Sound, Light and Interference
standard_text: Mechanical waves: transverse and longitudinal; amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period and v = fλ; sound, resonance and standing waves; reflection, refraction (Snell's law) and total internal reflection; diffraction, superposition and interference. (Senior Secondary Physics, Unit 2: Linear motion and waves)
meta_desc: Free Year 11 Physics worksheets on waves: transverse and longitudinal waves, v = fλ, sound, resonance, standing waves, refraction, Snell's law, total internal reflection and interference. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂.
body_html:
How to think about it

A wave transfers energy without transferring matter. In transverse waves particles vibrate at right angles to the direction of travel; in longitudinal waves (sound) they vibrate along it. For all waves v = fλ and f = 1/T.

Waves reflect, refract (change speed and direction), diffract and superpose. Two waves travelling in opposite directions make a standing wave with nodes and antinodes; driving a system at its natural frequency causes resonance. Light refracts according to Snell's law; beyond the critical angle there is total internal reflection.

Example

Sound at 340 m/s, frequency 680 Hz. Wavelength?

λ = v ÷ f = 340 ÷ 680

Answer: 0.50 m

Example

Light goes from air into glass (n = 1.50) at 30°. Angle of refraction?

sin r = sin 30° ÷ 1.50 = 0.333

Answer: 19.5°

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the frequency changes when a wave enters a new medium: speed and wavelength change.
  • Measuring angles from the surface instead of the normal.
  • Saying sound can travel through a vacuum.

faq.q: Why can you hear around a corner but not see around it?
faq.a: Sound waves have wavelengths of about a metre, similar to doorways, so they diffract a lot; light's wavelength is far too small.

faq.q: What is total internal reflection used for?
faq.a: Optical fibres carry internet and phone signals as light that reflects inside the glass core; it is also used in endoscopes.

items.q: What is resonance?

items.e: It is greatest when the gap is about one wavelength.

items.q: The same 200 Hz sound travels through glass (4540 m/s) and steel (5960 m/s). In which does it have the longer wavelength?
items.e: Same frequency: faster speed → longer wavelength.

items.q: The same 400 Hz sound travels through air (343 m/s) and steel (5960 m/s). In which does it have the longer wavelength?
